text: Last lesson covered the ASL skeleton. Now let's build a real one — a state machine with two Task states that runs a Glue job, then a Lambda function, in sequence.

ASL defines several state types, but four cover nearly every data pipeline. Task does work — invokes a Lambda, starts a Glue job. Choice branches on a condition, like an if-else inside the workflow. Parallel runs multiple branches at once and waits for all of them. Wait pauses for a fixed duration or until a timestamp.

This state machine starts a Glue ETL job, then invokes a Lambda to notify on success. Notice the Resource ends in "startJobRun.sync" rather than just "startJobRun" — that sync suffix tells Step Functions to actually wait for the Glue job to finish before moving to the next state, not just accept the start request.

By default, each state's full output becomes the next state's input. That's what lets the notify step know the Glue job succeeded — if the job had failed, execution would never reach it. Parameters is how you shape exactly what gets sent into the target service.
A real two-stage state machine, built. Next up: error handling — Catch and Retry, and what actually happens when a Task fails.
